note: Each proof declares its scope. 'generic' runs against any bot of this shape without changes. 'configurable' runs after the table and column names are set in audit.config.json. 'template' is a worked example tied to one specific bot — read it, then port it: the pattern is what matters, the identifiers are not.

exitCodes.2: the defect is absent — fixed, or it did not reproduce
exitCodes.3: not applicable to this subject — the precondition was not met

requires: a function that gates fulfilment on customer-supplied input
proofs.portability: Rename the function and the regex in the proof to match the bot under audit. The pattern to look for in any bot: a boolean gate that reads a field the customer typed, and whose result skips a payment step.

requires: an admin route that retries a digital purchase
proofs.portability: Points at two specific functions. The general pattern: a function returns a scalar, its caller reads a property from it, and the property check is always true.
P14 is the generic version of this class — it scans every module for the same pattern. Port P03 only if you need the per-request proof.

requires: a claims table linking a payment to an order
proofs.portability: Set moneyPath.bookingsTable, moneyPath.claimsTable and moneyPath.smsVerifiedColumn in audit.config.json.
Set moneyPath.couponRedemptionsTable. If the bot has no coupons, this proof reports NOT APPLICABLE.

requires: a fuzzy name matcher on the payment path
proofs.portability: Point the proof at the matcher exported by the bot under audit. The test pairs are generic Arabic names and need no change.
P15 is the generic version of this class — it validates every SQL column reference against the live schema. Prefer P15 on a new bot.
No configuration. Works on any Node project with a package.json.
Looks for the isTestEnvironment heuristic anywhere in src/. Works on any bot that derives its data directory from the environment.
Set lockFile in audit.config.json if the bot names it differently. The proof reads the live lock file and simulates the check.
Set moneyPath.refundsTable and moneyPath.customersTable. If the bot has no wallet, this proof reports NOT APPLICABLE.

requires: a claims table with unique indexes
proofs.portability: Set moneyPath.claimsTable and moneyPath.bookingsTable. This is the positive control — run it after every change to the payment path.
No configuration. Runs the bot's own npm test and npm run lint.
No configuration. Scans every module in src/ for an authenticator that accepts a request when its credential is missing.
No configuration. Extracts every column reference from every SQL string in src/ and validates it against the live schema.
No configuration. Finds catch blocks and floating promises that swallow an error without recording it.
